images.title: Balance the product rule
images.purpose: Recap the product rule as a balance: the HCF and LCM of 8 and 12 on one pan weigh the same as 8 and 12 on the other.
images.composition: One flat balance scale centred in the frame, level, with two blocks on each pan and a single equation line beneath, wide white margins.
exact_structure: One grey #6B7280 balance scale, centred, beam perfectly level.
Left pan: exactly 2 square blocks side by side, a reddish purple #CC79A7 block labelled HCF = 4 and a green #009E73 block labelled LCM = 24.
Right pan: exactly 2 square blocks side by side, a teal #0072B2 block labelled 8 and an amber #E69F00 block labelled 12.
A small × sign between the two blocks on each pan.
Below the scale, one bold centred line: 4 × 24 = 96 = 8 × 12.
Under that, one small grey caption: for two numbers only.
rejection: the beam tilted, or more or fewer than 2 blocks on either pan
an HCF other than 4, an LCM other than 24, or a product other than 96
three numbers placed on the right pan
images.takeaway: HCF × LCM balances the product of the two numbers, so knowing three of the four gives the fourth.
images.description: A level balance with HCF 4 and LCM 24 on one pan and 8 and 12 on the other, above 4 × 24 = 96 = 8 × 12.
images.context: Shown beside the practice tool on checking the product rule.
images.teaching_notes: Point out that the pans stay level, so if one block is hidden it can be found by dividing.

image_decisions.why: A balance gives a compact, memorable recap of the rule before the practice.
